title: Homily II — Laid in the tomb and taken up on the third day

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily II on the Dormition, cols. 740-741 (PDF leaves 411-412)

source_text: Ἐντεῦθεν πρὸς τὴν Γεθσημανῆ τὴν ἱερωτάτην κατάγεται· πάλιν τε ἀσπασμοὶ καὶ περιπλοκαὶ, καὶ πάλιν ἐγκώμια, ὕμνοι ἱεροὶ, καὶ ἀνακλήσεις καὶ δάκρυα, ἐξ ἀγωνίας καὶ πόθου κρουνοὶ ἱδρώτων περιῤῥεόμενοι· καὶ ἦν ἰδεῖν ἱδρῶτας καὶ δάκρυα τοῖς γεύμασιν ἁμιλλώμενα. Καὶ οὕτως τὸ πανάγιον σῶμα τῷ πανευκλεεῖ καὶ ὑπερφυεῖ ἐπιτίθεται μνήματι· κἀντεῦθεν τριταῖον πρὸς οὐρανίους δόμους μετεωρίζεται. Ἔδει γὰρ τοῦτο τὸ θεοπρεπὲς ἐνδιαίτημα τὴν ἀνόρυκτον πηγὴν τοῦ τῆς ἀφέσεως ὕδατος, τὴν ἀνήροτον ἄρουραν τοῦ οὐρανίου ἄρτου, τὴν ἀνάρδευτον ἄμπελον τοῦ τῆς ἀμβροσίας βότρυος, τὴν ἀειθαλῆ καὶ καλλίκαρπον ἐλαίαν τοῦ πατρικοῦ ἐλαίου, τοῖς κενεῶσι τῆς γῆς μὴ καθείργεσθαι· ἀλλ' ὥσπερ τὸ ἐξ αὐτῆς τῷ Θεῷ Λόγῳ ἐνυποστὰν σῶμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ ἀκήρατον, τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ μνήματος ἐξανίστατο, οὕτω δὴ καὶ ταύτην ἐξαρπασθῆναι τοῦ τάφου, καὶ πρὸς τὸν Υἱὸν τὴν μητέρα μεθαρμοσθῆναι, καὶ ὥσπερ αὐτὸς πρὸς αὐτὴν καταβέβηκεν, οὕτως αὐτὴν τὴν προφιλῆ πρὸς αὐτὴν ἀναφέρεσθαι, τὴν μείζονα καὶ τελειοτέραν σκηνὴν, εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν οὐρανόν. Ἔδει τὴν τὸν Θεὸν Λόγον ἐν τῇ αὐτῆς νηδύϊ ξενοδοχήσασαν, ἐν ταῖς τοῦ ἑαυτῆς Υἱοῦ κατοικισθῆναι σκηναῖς· καὶ ὥσπερ ὁ Κύριος ἔφησεν, ὡς ἐν τοῖς τοῦ οἰκείου Πατρὸς εἶναι ὀφείλεται, καὶ τὴν Μητέρα ἔδει ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Υἱοῦ βασιλείοις αὐλίζεσθαι, ἐν οἴκῳ Κυρίου, καὶ ἐν αὐλαῖς οἴκου Θεοῦ ἡμῶν. Εἰ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῷ πάντων τῶν εὐφραινομένων ἡ κατοικία, ποῦ τῆς εὐφροσύνης τὸ αἴτιον; Ἔδει τῆς ἐν τῷ τίκτειν φυλαξάσης τὴν παρθενίαν ἀλώβητον, ἀδιάφθορον τηρηθῆναι τὸ σῶμα, καὶ μετὰ θάνατον. Ἔδει τὴν ἐγκόλπιον ὡς βρέφος τὸν Κτίστην βαστάσασαν, τοῖς θείοις ἐνδιατρίβειν σκηνώμασιν. Ἔδει τὴν νύμφην, ἣν ὁ Πατὴρ ἐνυμφεύσατο, τοῖς οὐρανίοις ἐνδιαιτᾶσθαι θαλάμοις. Ἔδει τὴν ἐν σταυρῷ τὸν ἑαυτῆς Υἱὸν κατοπτεύσασαν, καὶ τῆς ὠδῖνος, ἣν τεκοῦσα διέφυγε, τὴν ῥομφαίαν δεξαμένην ἐγκάρδιον, τῷ Πατρὶ καθορᾷν συγκαθήμενον. Ἔδει τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ Μητέρα τὰ τοῦ Υἱοῦ κατακτήσασθαι, καὶ ὑπὸ πάσης ὡς Μητέρα Θεοῦ καὶ δούλην προσκυνηθῆναι τῆς κτίσεως. Ἀεὶ μὲν γὰρ ἐκ τῶν τεκόντων ὁ κλῆρος εἰς τοὺς παῖδας κάτεισι. Νῦν δὲ, ὥς τις ἔφη σοφὸς, ἄνω ποταμῶν τῶν ἱερῶν χωροῦσι πηγαί. Ὁ γὰρ Υἱὸς τῇ Μητρὶ τὴν σύμπασαν κτίσιν κατεδουλώσατο.
pass_a_gloss: From there to the most holy Gethsemane she is brought down (κατάγω); and again greetings/kisses (ἀσπασμοί) and embraces, and again encomia (ἐγκώμια), holy hymns, and invocations/callings-back and tears, from anguish (ἀγωνία) and longing (πόθος) streams (κρουνοί) of sweats (ἱδρῶτες) pouring around (περιρρέω); and it was possible to see sweats and tears vying with the [printed: tastes, γεύμασιν; read streams, ῥεύμασιν] [clause lacking in R.]. And so the all-holy body is placed in the all-glorious and supernatural (ὑπερφυής) monument/tomb (μνῆμα); and from there on the third day (τριταῖον) to heavenly houses (δόμοι) it is raised aloft. For it was necessary/fitting (ἔδει) that this God-befitting dwelling, the undug spring (πηγή) of the water (ὕδωρ) of remission/forgiveness (ἄφεσις), the unploughed (ἀνήροτος) field (ἄρουρα) of the heavenly bread (ἄρτος), the unwatered vine (ἄμπελος) of the cluster (βότρυς) of ambrosia (ἀμβροσία), the ever-blooming (ἀειθαλής) and fair-fruited olive (ἐλαία) of the paternal (πατρικόν) oil, not be shut in (καθείργω) by the hollows (κενεῶνες) of the earth; but as the body from her, enhypostatized in God the Word, the holy and undefiled, on the third day rose from the tomb, so also she [must] be snatched (ἐξαρπάζω) from the grave (τάφος), and the mother be transferred/joined to the Son, and as he came down to her, so she the beloved (προφιλής) be carried up (ἀναφέρω) to it [printed πρὸς αὐτήν; R. πρὸς αὐτόν], the greater and more perfect tabernacle (σκηνή), into heaven itself. It was fitting that she who received as guest God the Word in her womb (νηδύς) be settled in the tabernacles (σκηναί) of her own Son; and as the Lord said that he ought to be in the [things/house] of his own Father, so also the Mother must lodge in the palaces (βασίλεια) of the Son, in the house of the Lord, and in the courts (αὐλαί) of the house of our God. For if in it [is] the dwelling (κατοικία) of all who rejoice, where [is] the cause (αἴτιον) of gladness? It was fitting that of her who in giving birth (τίκτω) guarded (φυλάσσω) virginity (παρθενία) unharmed (ἀλώβητος), the body be kept (τηρέω) incorrupt also after death (θάνατος). It was fitting that she who carried (βαστάζω) the Creator (Κτίστης) in her bosom (ἐγκόλπιος) as a babe (βρέφος) spend her time in the divine tabernacles (σκηνώματα). It was fitting that the bride (νύμφη) whom the Father betrothed live in the heavenly bridal chambers (θάλαμοι). It was fitting that she who looked upon (κατοπτεύω) her own Son on the cross (σταυρός), and received in her heart (ἐγκάρδιος) the sword (ῥομφαία) of the birth-pang (ὠδίς) which in giving birth she escaped (διαφεύγω), behold (καθοράω) him sitting with the Father. It was fitting that the Mother of God acquire the [things] of the Son, and be venerated (προσκυνέω) by all creation (κτίσις) as Mother of God and handmaid (δούλη). For always from the parents the inheritance (κλῆρος) goes down (κάτειμι) to the children (παῖδες); but now, as some wise man (σοφός) said, upward (ἄνω) go (χωρέω) the springs of the sacred rivers (ποταμοί). For the Son made subject the whole creation to the Mother.
pass_b_english: From there she is brought down to most holy Gethsemane. Again there were kisses and embraces, and again praises, holy hymns, invocations and tears, and streams of sweat poured down from anguish and longing; one could see sweat and tears vying with each other in their flowing. And so the all-holy body is laid in the all-glorious and wondrous tomb, and from there, on the third day, it is lifted up to the halls of heaven.

For it was fitting that this dwelling worthy of God, the spring of the water of forgiveness, which no one dug; the unploughed field of the heavenly bread; the unwatered vine of the cluster of ambrosia; the evergreen and fruitful olive tree of the Father's mercy, should not be shut up in the hollows of the earth. Rather, just as the holy and undefiled body, which came from her and took its subsistence in God the Word, rose from the tomb on the third day, so she too had to be snatched from the tomb, and the Mother brought over to her Son; and as he had come down to her, so she, the dearly loved, had to be carried up to the greater and more perfect tabernacle, into heaven itself (Hebrews 9:11; Hebrews 9:24).

It was fitting that she who had welcomed God the Word as a guest in her womb should be settled in the dwellings of her own Son; and as the Lord said that he must be in the house of his own Father (Luke 2:49), so the Mother too had to make her home in the palace of her Son, in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God (Psalm 135:2). For if the dwelling of all who rejoice is there (Psalm 87:7), where should the cause of joy be? It was fitting that she who kept her virginity unharmed in giving birth should have her body kept incorrupt even after death. It was fitting that she who carried the Creator as an infant in her bosom should abide in the divine tabernacles. It was fitting that the bride whom the Father had espoused should live in the bridal chambers of heaven. It was fitting that she who had seen her own Son on the cross, and had received into her heart the sword of the pain she had escaped in giving birth (Luke 2:35), should behold him seated with the Father. It was fitting that the Mother of God should possess what belongs to her Son, and be venerated by all creation as the Mother and handmaid of God. For the inheritance always passes down from parents to children; but now, as a wise man said, the springs of the sacred rivers flow upward. For the Son has made all creation subject to his Mother.

choices.note: "The greater and more perfect tabernacle" is the wording of Hebrews 9:11, and "into heaven itself" of Hebrews 9:24; both cited.
Luke 2:49 (ἐν τοῖς τοῦ πατρός μου) rendered "in the house of his own Father", which suits the parallel "palace of her Son".

The printed margin reads "Psal. cxxxii, 2"; the words "in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God" are Psalm 134:2 LXX (also in LXX 133:1) = Psalm 135:2 in English numbering, cited so.
"The dwelling of all who rejoice" is Psalm 86:7 LXX = Psalm 87:7 (English numbering); the LXX wording (spoken of Zion) differs from Hebrew-based English versions.
"The sword" is Simeon's word in Luke 2:35; cited.
Doctrine kept exactly: the body is laid in the tomb and on the third day lifted up to heaven (τριταῖον ...
μετεωρίζεται); she escaped the pains of labour in giving birth and received the sword at the cross.

Printed ἐλαίου ("oil") is rendered "mercy": the edition's note (52) says "omnino legendum ἐλέου, ut Lipomanus" and the PG Latin has "paternae miserationis olivam"; the olive/mercy wordplay (ἐλαία / ἔλεος) also stands in Psalm 52:8 (LXX 51:10), uncited.

Printed γεύμασιν ("tastes") makes no sense with "vying"; read as ῥεύμασιν ("streams") with the PG Latin "fluentis", rendered "vying with each other in their flowing"; the edition notes (50) that this clause is lacking in R.
Printed πρὸς αὐτὴν ...
σκηνήν is taken in apposition ("to the greater ... tabernacle");
(53) R. reads πρὸς αὐτόν ("to him") and adds καθαρωτέραν ("purer").
The source notes record this reading as doubtful.
Gethsemane, ἀγωνία and sweat may recall Luke 22:44; possible echo, left uncited.
ἄνω ποταμῶν ἱερῶν χωροῦσι παγαί is Euripides, Medea 410 ("as a wise man said"); not Scripture, uncited.
ἐνυποστάν rendered "took its subsistence in", as in Homily I.
ἀνακλήσεις ("callings upon" or "callings back") rendered "invocations".
προσκυνηθῆναι rendered "be venerated" (honour, not the worship due to God).
"The Mother and handmaid of God" keeps the Greek pairing ὡς Μητέρα Θεοῦ καὶ δούλην.
Other variants: (51) ὑπερφυεῖ: R.
ὑπερυεῖ (a misprint);
(54) ἐνδιαιτᾶσθαι: R.
ἐνδιατρίβειν (same sense).
Review confirmed printed γεύμασιν on the page image (leaf 411, col. 740); the emendation to ῥεύμασιν rests on sense and the PG Latin "fluentis suis".
μεθαρμοσθῆναι ("be moved over, transferred") rendered "brought over" (PG Latin "ad Filium migrare").
Printed πρὸς αὐτὴν ἀναφέρεσθαι confirmed on leaf 412; the PG Latin ("ad majus praestantiusque tabernaculum, hoc est, ad ipsum caelum") supports the appositional reading.
